Hi Samir / Lena — thanks for carving out the time today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and so your infra/infra-sre folks have something to work from.

TL;DR
- Pain: real-time claim-processing (90% of flows) is highly latency-sensitive — current infra struggles at peak volume; false fallbacks to batch degrade experience.
- Goal: POC to validate p95 latency <= 75ms for short-chat workflows (context ~512 tokens), and sustained throughput ~180–220 QPS for the inference path.
- Proposed runbook: 4-week POC, dedicated capacity with canary traffic, periodic metrics handoff.

What we heard (confirm/correct):
- Primary flow: short chat completions (prompt+context ≤ 512 tokens) for claims triage; a smaller set (~15%) are longer context batches (1,500–2,000 tokens) for policy drafting.
- Traffic: baseline 30 QPS, expected peak bursts ~220 QPS (5–10 min bursts during morning syncs).
- Latency goal: p95 <= 75ms for short-chat (user-facing), p99 planning for <200ms with graceful degradation.
- Security: PII in prompts — you’ll run POC on Redwood Dedicated in your VPC (preferred) or our Private appliance if needed.

Action items / next steps (by owner):
1) AuroraEdge: share a 24h traffic dump + representative prompt set (Samir) — needed by Friday 8/7.
2) Redwood (me + Karthik): provide topology options (dedicated pool sizing, fallback variants, cache config) and a preliminary cost estimate by Tuesday 8/10.
3) Schedule a 60min ops deep-dive for your SRE team (propose 8/11 or 8/12).

Technical constraints / considerations we flagged on the call:
- Prefer quantized variants for cost (4-bit/8-bit) but must validate functional parity for the policy drafting flows.
- KV cache/prefix caching is essential for chat sessions — we’ll instrument to measure cache hit-rate impact on p95.
- Autoscale warm-up for bursts — suggest a small standby buffer (20% surge capacity) in the dedicated pool to absorb sub-minute spikes.

Attachments: draft POC MOP attached (auroraedge-poc-mop.pdf). I also included a sample latency trace we can compare against once you send the traffic dump.

If this looks good I’ll kick off the internal ops alignment and circulate the topology options.

Thanks,

Chloe / Samir — quick technical sketch based on the thread and the constraints you called out. This is intended as an initial recommendation for the POC; we’ll baseline with actual traffic once we ingest the sample.

POC goals restated (for design):
- Short-chat p95 <= 75ms (context <= 512 tokens)
- Sustained throughput validated up to 220 QPS, with a 1-hour stress at 120% peak for the SLA test (per request)

Option A — Dedicated VPC pool (low friction, higher unit cost):
- Fleet: 6xA100-80GB (GPU) – configured into 3 shards for redundancy.
- Model set: primary = quantized 8-bit variant of your selected open model (validate accuracy), fallback = 8B dense/quantized small model for degraded load.
- Runtime: continuous batching with latency-aware max batch size of 32 for short-chat (empirically ≈ 40–65ms per token under ideal conditions).
- Cache: per-session KV cache with a global prefix cache for repeated prompts; expect cache hit-rate > 60% for short-chat after warm-up.
- Autoscale: keep a 20% headroom buffer (pre-warmed instances) + rapid scale-up policy keyed to 30s moving-average of queue depth.
- Canary: 10% traffic, 30m monitoring window, automatic rollback on error rate > 1% or p95 regress > 20ms.

Option B — Mixed-cost pool (lower cost, slightly more complex):
- Fleet: 4xA100 + 2xL4 (NVIDIA L4 equivalency) where L4 serves longer-context and background queued jobs.
- Routing: short-chat -> A100 pool; long-context or cheaper path -> L4 pool; fallback model (4B quantized) available if sustained system-wide QPS > 250 for > 5 minutes.
- Model quantization: recommend start with 8-bit for policy-drafting eval — if eval shows parity run a 4-bit pass on a secondary model and A/B on small test set.
- Batching: dynamic batching with per-request latency cap; smaller max-batch for short-chat to protect p95.

POC SLA test (as requested):
- Simulate 1 hour at 120% of observed peak (≈ 264 QPS) using your anonymized prompt corpus + synthetic bursts; measure p95/p99, cache hit-rate, GPU utilization, and cross-az network overhead.
- Rollback criteria: sustained p95 > 120ms or error rate > 2%.

Operational notes / risks:
- Quantization risk: 4-bit may introduce subtle regressions in policy-drafting tasks — we’ll define model-sensitivity tests (100 curated prompts) to score factuality and hallucination. If regression > 3% vs baseline, keep 8-bit.
- KV cache eviction policies will materially affect p95 for session-heavy flows; recommend LRU with per-session affinity for the POC.
- Networking: for Dedicated in your VPC we’ll share IP ranges and set up a VPN/peering. KMS integration: we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS; will provide required docs in the security packet.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short topology sketch and estimated cost deltas (ballpark) to the shared POC folder (auroraedge-poc-mop.pdf, sample-latency-trace.json).

Next steps:
- Chloe: confirm which topology to present to AuroraEdge SRE in tomorrow’s ops session.
- Samir: send the 24h dump + prompts so we can run sizing with real distribution.

Will follow with a more detailed node-level sizing if you confirm Option A or B.

Thanks — Karthik
